newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Soccer-Four teams withdraw from African cups.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Four teams withdraw from African cups.

text.p: Clubs from Ghana, Mozambique, Namibia and South Africa have announced late withdrawals from this weekend's African club competition matches, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) said on Wednesday.
Three of the four withdrawals have come in the CAF Cup while Ghana's Hearts of Oak have pulled out of their scheduled match against ASFAG of Guinea in the African Cup Winners' Cup.
The CAF Cup withdrawals are Umtata Bucks of South Africa, Mozambique's Textil do Pungue and the Namibian club Chief Santos.
Bucks were due to play Centre Chiefs of Botswana while Textil do Pungue's withdrawal gives C and M Sales of Swaziland a free passage into the second round in May.
Joining them will be Kabwe Warriors of Zambia who were due to play Chief Santos.
The clubs cited lack of financial resources for the withdrawals but they will all be subject to fines from CAF.
